newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SACCHI SAYS MILAN'S TITLE HOPES VIRTUALLY DEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SACCHI SAYS MILAN'S TITLE HOPES VIRTUALLY DEAD.

text.p: Coach Arrigo Sacchi on Saturday accused many of his AC Milan players of being mentally absent, saying the team's hopes of retaining the Italian league title were practically dead as leaders Juventus looked unstoppable.

Asked if he believed Milan could cut the eight-point gap which separates them from European champions Juventus, Sacchi told Corriere dello Sport daily: "Not at all...Juventus are the most organised club in Europe at the moment."
Former Italy manager Sacchi said Milan's problems were mainly mental, with many of his players lacking motivation after years of success.
"It is crazy to compare this Milan with the one I coached in 1988 which made up precious lost points on Napoli late in the season to win the title," Sacchi was quoted as saying.
"That team had come from 10 years of failures, this one has come from 10 years of success."

Sacchi, who spent five glorious years at Milan until his appointment to the national side in 1991, returned to the club earlier this month after Uruguayan coach Oscar Tabarez resigned following a poor start to the season.

But Sacchi, who was hugely unpopular as Italy coach despite taking them to the final of the 1994 World Cup, has had a hard time so far at Milan, who were eliminated from the European Cup in his first match back and lost to strugglers Parma last Sunday.
He said he was not worried that striker George Weah and defender Paolo Maldini would miss Milan's next match at Lazio on January 5 because of injury.
"What worries me is that too many players who are present are actually 'absent'," said Sacchi. "In reality, we are not yet a team -- we are merely a sort of representative group and nothing more."
